There are several ways to ask for help in English. You can use polite and casual language to do this. Let's look at one particular structure for asking for help.

You can use the structure
Can/ Could + you + show/ tell + me + question word

Let me tell you what you should do.
Discussing How to Deal with Problems
To discuss how to deal with problems such as computer connection problems, you can use modals like might, could, or should.
These modals can go at the beginning of the sentence, or after a clause starting with "If ... "
The modal is followed by a verb in the base form. You do not use “to”.

images.text:
Rachel: Hello, this is Rachel from InternetPlus. How may I help you?
Vanessa: I need to speak with someone about my Internet connection.
Rachel: Absolutely! What seems to be the problem?
Vanessa: Do you know how to connect a new modem?
I just purchased a new one and I can't seem to get the Internet to work.
Rachel: Before you start, you should read the manual.
Vanessa: Hmm … I forgot, sorry.

Rachel: No problem. I would start by connecting all the cords and turning on the modem first, followed by the computer.
Vanessa: Hmmm ... alright. Could you tell me where to plug in the Ethernet cable? All these cables look the same to me.
Rachel: The ethernet cable goes in a large socket on the side of your computer. It should be blue.
Vanessa: Found it! OK, done. Let me see what happens. Oh goodness ... Can you explain what to do now that the green light on the modem is flashing?

Rachel: Don't worry ... that means that it's trying to connect to the Internet provider. Give it a minute. Also, I wouldn't try to connect to the Wi-Fi until you are confident that the modem is working properly.
Vanessa: I understand. The green light has stopped flashing. I'm going to log in and see if I can go online. Yeah! I'm in!
Rachel: Is there anything else I can help you with? You could receive monthly e-mails about online tips and tricks, if you are interested.
Vanessa: No, thank you. You've been very helpful.

Instructions:
Imagine you have just bought a new piece of technological equipment, but it is not working properly.
You have to call a customer service representative.
Write a 10-12 line dialogue between you and a customer service representative.
Explain the problem in detail. Ask questions using how to, where to and what to.
Include suggestions about how to deal with these problems. Use should, would and could.
Remember to write in complete sentences. Add question marks to the end of sentences for questions.
When you have typed in ALL your answers, click the Go to Writing Task button.
